title: Monomial-ideal tensor injectivity in a log regular chart
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid, written additively, let $A$ be a commutative ring, and let $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$ be a chart making $\operatorname{Spec}A$ a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Write $\mathbf Z[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}\mathbf Zz^p$, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, and give $A$ its $\mathbf Z[P]$-algebra structure $z^p\mapsto\alpha(p)$. For every monoid ideal $H\subset P$ (meaning $H+P\subset H$), write $\mathbf Z[H]=\bigoplus_{h\in H}\mathbf Zz^h$, an ideal of $\mathbf Z[P]$. Then the multiplication map
$$A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[H]\longrightarrow A,\qquad a\otimes z^h\longmapsto a\alpha(h),$$
is injective and has image the ideal $(\alpha(h):h\in H)$ of $A$. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.4.3, printed p. 110, using Kato 1994, 6.1(ii); 3.5, printed p. 115, explicitly states the monomial Tor-independence theorem.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point x of Spec A and write A_x for the local ring and A_x^{sh} for its strict henselization. Let F be the face of P consisting of elements whose images in A_x are units, put P_F={p-f}, and put P_x=P_F/F^{gp}. The face-sharpening statement [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] gives the fine saturated sharp quotient and the splitting P_F≅P_x⊕F^{gp}; the sharp-chart statement [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart] supplies an etale-local chart b:P_x→A_x^{sh} inducing the characteristic identification. Apply [lem-trf-log-chart-face-tor-comparison] to the localized chart α:P→A_x^{sh}. It explicitly supplies the localization at F, the chosen section, the unit homomorphism u with α∘s=u·b, and the change-of-rings identification, carrying the ideal generated by H to the image ideal H_x. Thus, for R=Z[P] and I=Z[H], it identifies Tor^R_1(R/I,A_x^{sh}) with Tor^{Z[P_x]}_1(Z[P_x]/Z[H_x],A_x^{sh}). The latter vanishes by [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart].

source.place: Expose VI, 3.7(a), printed p. 75, and Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.4.3, printed p. 110; Kato (1994), 6.1(ii).

proof.text:
For the same R and I, let x lie over the prime $\mathfrak p$ of A, so $A_x=A_{\mathfrak p}$ is the local ring of Spec A at the image point. It is Noetherian: Spec A is locally Noetherian, so $A_x$ is a localization of a Noetherian ring $D$ of an affine open, and every ideal of a localization $S^{-1}D$ is the extension of an ideal of $D$ (Stacks 00FN; elementary). Hence [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr], applied to Y=Spec A and the geometric point x, says that the canonical map $\iota:A_x\to A_x^{sh}=\mathcal O^{sh}_{\operatorname{Spec}A,x}$ (the same strict henselization of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] used in Step 1 and in [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart]) is a flat local homomorphism, so it is faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective]. The R-algebra structure of $A_x^{sh}$ through $\iota$ is the localized chart of Step 1. Apply [lem-trf-tor-flat-base-change] to $R\to A_x\to A_x^{sh}$ to obtain
$$Tor^R_1(R/I,A_x)\otimes_{A_x}A_x^{sh}\cong Tor^R_1(R/I,A_x^{sh}).$$
The right side is zero by Step 1, so [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-tensor-zero] gives Tor^R_1(R/I,A_x)=0. The coefficient-localization statement [lem-trf-tor-localization-on-spec] identifies the localization of Tor^R_1(R/I,A) at the prime $\mathfrak p$ with Tor^R_1(R/I,A_{\mathfrak p})=Tor^R_1(R/I,A_x)=0; since every prime of A is the image of a geometric point, the global Tor module is zero.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00M8 (flat base change for the free-resolution computation), Tag 00HR (flat local homomorphisms are faithfully flat), Tag 00HP (faithfully flat reflection), Tag 00FN (localization of a Noetherian ring), and the localization consequence of the same free-resolution argument; flatness of the strict henselization as in More on Algebra Tag 07QM.

proof.text: Choose a projective resolution of R/I over R as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] to the short exact sequence 0→I→R→R/I→0 with N=A. Since R is projective, Tor^R_1(R,A)=0, and the exact sequence identifies Tor^R_1(R/I,A) with the kernel of I⊗_R A→R⊗_R A. Step 2 therefore makes I⊗_R A→R⊗_R A injective. Under R⊗_R A≅A and the basis elements z^h of Z[H]⊂I, this map is the displayed multiplication map A⊗_R Z[H]→A.

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00LY and 00M0/00M3; the low-degree Tor exact sequence for 0→I→R→R/I→0.

proof.text: The image is generated by the pure tensors a⊗z^h, whose images are aα(h), so it is exactly the ideal (α(h):h∈H). If H is empty, both the tensor source and this generated ideal are zero.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.4.3, printed p. 110, invoking Kato (1994), 6.1(ii); local-to-global descent made explicit using Stacks Tag 00M8 and Tag 00HP.

mathlib_searches.query: For a log regular scheme with monoid chart P, tensoring the inclusion of any monomial ideal of the integer monoid ring with the chart algebra remains injective.
Kato Tor independence for monomial ideals in a log regular chart gives Tor one of Z[P]/I with A equal to zero.

lean.statement: theorem logRegular_monomialIdeal_tensor_injective (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (eA : X.scheme ≅ Spec (.of A)) (hlog : X.IsLogRegular) (P : Type u) [AddCommMonoid P] (hP : IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Multiplicative P)) (α : Multiplicative P →* A) (c : Multiplicative P →* X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X.scheme)))) (hc : X.logStructure.IsChart (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X.scheme)) c) (hα : ∀ p : P, X.logStructure.alpha.app (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X.scheme))) (c (Multiplicative.ofAdd p)) = eA.hom.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv (α (Multiplicative.ofAdd p)))) [Algebra (MonoidAlgebra ℤ (Multiplicative P)) A] (hAlg : algebraMap (MonoidAlgebra ℤ (Multiplicative P)) A = (MonoidAlgebra.lift ℤ A (Multiplicative P) α).toRingHom) (H : Set P) (hH : ∀ h ∈ H, ∀ p : P, h + p ∈ H) : Function.Injective (LinearMap.liftBaseChange A ((Algebra.linearMap (MonoidAlgebra ℤ (Multiplicative P)) A).comp (Ideal.span {z : MonoidAlgebra ℤ (Multiplicative P) | ∃ h ∈ H, z = MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd h) 1}).subtype)) ∧ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.liftBaseChange A ((Algebra.linearMap (MonoidAlgebra ℤ (Multiplicative P)) A).comp (Ideal.span {z : MonoidAlgebra ℤ (Multiplicative P) | ∃ h ∈ H, z = MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd h) 1}).subtype)) = (Ideal.span ((fun h : P ↦ α (Multiplicative.ofAdd h)) '' H) : Submodule A A)
